blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 30 in June to 35 in October (+16.7%), and it took 7.1% of the city’s 294 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings rose from 22 in June to 27 in October (+22.7%), and it took 2.4% of the city’s 456 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out Pacific Douglas for detached houses in September, October (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in July, August (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in August (a buyers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Lots and land in Pacific Douglas
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Summerfield — detached freehold houses, not a strata complex: a detached-house subdivision name on the feed (172 / 172a / 171a Streets); a current listing describes a four-bedroom house "Welcome to Summerfield!" on 172 Street. It is the area's fee-simple lot fabric — detached houses on fee-simple lots — and no Summerfield condo or land-subdivision offering exists to count.

Assembly / development site — documented as such, never as inventory: the 172 Street / 2 Avenue five-lot cluster (148, 158, 172, 186, 192 172 Street): Five feed cards, each marketed in listing text as hold-or-develop land with the neighbouring properties also for sale as an assembly, quoting the Douglas NCP "Commercial/Residential" designation and an OCP "Urban" designation for the corner. The cluster is one negotiation, not five lots of inventory; diligence and pricing run on the combined parcel set and its current OCP/zoning position, and no asking figure is carried here.
Lot character, only: no Pacific Douglas lot-size or zone schedule is stated — the zone of a specific lot is not verified until checked parcel by parcel under Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000.

ALR vs non-ALR: the plan area is bordered by the Agricultural Land Reserve to the north — the north-edge lots are the ALR check. Whether a specific parcel is in the ALR is not verified at parcel level; check the parcel in the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder, and any ALR parcel follows the ALC frame in.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Pacific Douglas

items.t: The City's Douglas NCP page confirms the City name and frame: "Douglas is the name of Surrey's most southern urban neighbourhood. It is located between the Peach Arch and Pacific border crossing adjacent to the United States.

City plan area versus board sub-area — different geographies: the Douglas plan encompasses approximately 61 hectares (150 acres), generally east of Hwy 99, west of Hwy 15 and north of the United States, bordered by the Agricultural Land Reserve and the Glades Garden Park to the north; the planning process concluded in 1999. The board sub-area's feed reaches 18/19 Avenue and 4 Avenue addresses north of that old NCP pocket, and the street-level board boundary is not verified — FVREB publishes none, and the NCP area was not substituted for it.

Board geography: "Pacific Douglas" is one of nine sub-areas of the Fraser Valley board community "S Surrey White Rock" (Crescent Beach Ocean Park, Elgin Chantrell, Grandview, Hazelmere, King George Corridor, Morgan Creek, Pacific Douglas, Sunnyside Park, White Rock). (As of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report.)
Peace Arch Hospital, 15521 Russell Avenue, White Rock, is a Fraser Health community hospital providing emergency, surgery and maternity care, open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

Market context, labelled correctly: SnapStats covers S Surrey White Rock. Community context only (SnapStats publishes medians at community level only; land has no SnapStats category): S Surrey White Rock Detached median $1,628,000, $545/sq ft, 102% sale-to-list, 30 days; "Condos & Townhomes" combined median $700,000, $524/sq ft, 99%, 33 days. (As of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report.)

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Pacific Douglas

items.t: OCP — Surrey Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 21900 ("Surrey 2050," adopted June 15, 2026) is the current plan; Bylaw No. 18020 is the replaced predecessor. The City states the Douglas NCP's land use designations "have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 – Official Community Plan Update corporate report" — the in-force check for any Douglas lot is the Surrey 2050 designation plus the lot's zone, not the 1999 NCP designations that listing text still quotes.
Zoning — Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000: parcel by parcel.

Subdivision + servicing — Surrey Subdivision and Development Bylaw, 1986, No. 8830 (verified on the City's own pages): the bylaw under which subdivision and servicing requirements for a Douglas parcel run; parcel-level requirements are confirmed with the City.

SSMUH as Surrey states it (in effect July 8, 2024): Surrey's small-scale multi-unit housing framework under Zoning By-law No. 12000 — a maximum of 3 units on lots smaller than 280 m², 4 units on lots larger than 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop, applying to eligible residential lots under 4,050 m² inside the Urban Containment Boundary. Confirm the parcel's eligibility before pricing in added units.

Secondary suites (Surrey frame): one secondary suite may be permitted in a single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling, its habitable floor area may not exceed 40% of the principal dwelling unit's habitable area under Zoning By-law No. 12000, and it can never be a separate strata lot; the old 90 m² Surrey suite cap is not a current rule — never state it. A feed card's "licenced revenue suite" wording (259 172a Street) is a claim to verify against City records, not a fact.

Coach houses and garden suites (Surrey frame): permitted in residential zones that allow detached houses, duplexes and houseplexes; 35 m² minimum and 75 m² maximum, rising to a maximum of 120 m² for lots zoned RA, R2, R2-O and R3 where the principal dwelling has not achieved its maximum floor area.
Streamside setbacks: in Part 7A of Zoning By-law No. 12000, varying by stream class — no single riparian figure is ever stated for Surrey ground.

Short-term rentals (Surrey frame): permitted, owner-only — an owner must host from their principal residence and hold a City business licence at $358/yr (Zoning By-law No. 12000, Part 4 s. B.7(d); Business License By-law No. 13680, s. 60.1), with the City's 2024 corporate report's $350/yr proposal disclosed as a conflict — carry $358 with $350 disclosed, and check the City licence page before quoting either figure.

ALR block (ALR ground borders the plan area to the north; parcel status not verified per lot): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31).

Bare-land strata block (for the form — no Pacific Douglas bare-land strata plan is verified): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

blocks.text: Good to know about Pacific Douglas

items.t: The 1999 plan still quoted in listings no longer governs: the Douglas NCP's designations were superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP — yet the five-lot 172 Street assembly cards quote the NCP "Commercial/Residential" designation. Read development value off the in-force OCP (Bylaw No. 21900) and the Bylaw No. 12000 zone for the PID, not the listing text.

The board sub-area is bigger than the City neighbourhood: the City's Douglas plan area is about 61 hectares east of Highway 99, west of Highway 15 and north of the border — but the board feed under "Pacific Douglas" reaches 18/19 Avenue and 4 Avenue addresses well north of that pocket (Berkeley Village at 16433 19 Avenue among them, with listing sources split between Pacific Douglas and Grandview filings). A "Pacific Douglas" label is a board filing, not a City boundary.
They look alike in a search thumbnail and are opposite in law.

Sewer coverage here has a dated, partial official record: a 2007 City corporate report states a City sanitary sewer system services about half the Douglas lands, flowing to the Douglas sanitary pump station; current parcel-level servicing is not verified — a material check on the area's older streets before pricing subdivision or suite potential.

blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in Pacific Douglas
Local rules that affect duplexes in Pacific Douglas

items.t: Plan and zoning (Surrey): The in-force check for any Douglas lot is the Surrey 2050 OCP designation (OCP Bylaw 21900, adopted Jun 15, 2026 — never 18020-as-current) plus the lot's zone under Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000 — not the 1999 Douglas NCP designations that listing text still quotes, which the City states have been superseded. SSMUH position (Surrey, Jul 8, 2024): Duplexes are the baseline small-scale multi-unit form. Coach houses and garden suites in Surrey: Permitted in residential zones that allow detached houses, duplexes and houseplexes; 35 m² minimum and 75 m² maximum, rising to a maximum of 120 m² for lots zoned RA, R2, R2-O and R3 where the principal dwelling has not achieved its maximum floor area. Servicing Bylaw 8830 (1986) verified. Streamside setbacks sit in Part 7A of Zoning 12000 and vary by stream class — no single riparian figure is ever stated.

ALR edge: The plan area is bordered by the ALR to the north; any parcel in the ALR follows the ALC housing frame of one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m² plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha).

faq.a: No verified lot offering exists — no named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata plan or presale lot offering was verified.
faq.q: Can I buy a vacant lot in Pacific Douglas?

faq.a: No. The 1999 Douglas NCP designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP (Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026); check the in-force OCP designation and the Bylaw No. 12000 zone for the specific PID. The 148–192 172 Street assembly's current designation is not verified.
faq.q: A listing quotes a Douglas NCP designation for development potential — can I rely on it?

faq.a: Treat it as one: the cards themselves state the neighbouring properties are also for sale as an assembly — price and diligence run on the combined parcel set and its current OCP/zoning position, not on any single lot's asking figure.
faq.q: Is the five-lot 172 Street cluster five separate purchases?

faq.a: One suite per single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling, capped at 40% of the principal dwelling unit's habitable area under Zoning By-law No. 12000, never a separate strata lot. The old 90 m² cap is not a current rule.
faq.q: How big can a secondary suite be on a Douglas lot?

faq.a: Not verified parcel by parcel — the plan area borders the ALR to the north, and ALR status changes what can be built, subdivided and stratified; confirm the specific parcel in the ALC map finder, not the street.
faq.q: Is my north-edge lot in the ALR?

faq.a: It is not 55+, carries GST as new construction, and sits under redma's 7-day rescission and s.18 trust rules.
faq.q: Is Harlowe Pacific Douglas stock I can buy now?

faq.a: Douglas Point, by contrast, states not age-restricted — do not confuse the two rancher complexes.
faq.q: What about Eagles and The Greens at Douglas?

faq.a: Surrey permits one secondary suite in a single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling, capped at 40% of the principal dwelling's habitable area — Surrey's own rule. The old 90 m² cap is not current. Verify any existing suite claim against City records.
faq.q: Can I add a suite to a Pacific Douglas duplex?

faq.a: No — the 1999 NCP designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP. Check the in-force OCP designation and the Bylaw 12000 zone for the parcel before valuing development potential.
